title: Eval case
description: One question with a declared expected outcome. See README.md.

note.description: Why this case exists / the trap it sets.

requires.description: Injected context the expected answer DEPENDS on. Where a rung does not supply it, the case stops demanding a particular answer and only requires that the agent did not guess: a refusal or a clarification is then also correct.

metric.description: The governed metric the answer must come from.

gold_sql.description: Independent raw-SQL oracle for the number.

no_governed_metric.description: Declares that the layer has NO governed metric for this question, so `metric` is absent on purpose. Study-local only; the frozen set must always name its metric (tests/test_grade.py). Never set alongside `metric`.

gold_sql.description: Provenance only (the trap value); NOT graded as the answer.

reason.description: The code a REFUSAL must carry to be correct. A clarifying question is equally correct; a served number is still a miss.

oneOf.description: k >= 2: two or more GOVERNED definitions answer this question and all of them are defensible. Clarifying is correct; refusing is an over-refusal, because something does answer it; serving one number without disclosure is the silent error the case exists to catch. Each candidate declares its own oracle, so which one was served is recoverable and the miss can be priced by the gap between them.

concept.description: The concept the question names, in the words a person would use. The candidates are the governed definitions that claim it.

candidates.description: Every governed definition that legitimately answers. Hand-verified, independently of any detector — a pile whose labels come from the tool that gates at runtime proves nothing.

gold_sql.description: Independent raw-SQL oracle for THIS reading. Never the semantic layer.

owner.description: Who decides this definition. A candidate with no owner is a leftover, not a contested definition.

consumer.description: What downstream would break if this definition were deleted. This is the test of whether the ambiguity is irreducible.

tolerance.description: Tighter than elsewhere by default: attributing a served number to one candidate requires a band narrower than the gap between them.
